company_items.summary: AutoZone beat FQ4 EPS estimates ($56.05 vs. $54.03 consensus), but the quality was low — the beat was driven by tariff refunds (145 basis point GM tailwind) and a non-cash LIFO benefit (105 basis point tailwind). Domestic comps missed badly at +1.6% vs. +3.1% expected, and the operating expense ratio rose 100 basis points year-over-year. Positively, management noted improving sales linearity in the final 8 weeks and expressed confidence heading into fiscal 2027.

Cognex announced the acquisition of RealSense, a market leader in depth-sensing cameras and vision technology for robotic perception and Physical AI, for approximately $500 million upfront plus an additional ~$106.5 million. RealSense is expected to generate $80-90 million in revenue, representing more than 50% year-over-year growth. The deal positions Cognex directly in the fast-growing robotics and Physical AI supply chain.

MillerKnoll posted a solid FQ1 EPS beat (53 cents vs. 36 cents expected), and notably would have beaten even excluding an 11-cent tariff refund tailwind (42 cents ex-refunds vs. 36 cents consensus). Sales missed, declining 3.3% organically to $923.4 million vs. $943.2 million expected, though orders rose 3.5% year-over-year. Fiscal 2027 sales guidance was trimmed slightly but EPS guidance was left unchanged, and FQ2 EPS guidance is in line with consensus.

Pentair named Bob Hau as its new CFO effective November 1, with current interim CFO Bob Fishman staying on to ensure a smooth transition. Hau brings extensive experience as a former CFO at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox International. This is a leadership/operational update with no financial results accompanying the announcement.

THOR Industries missed FQ4 EPS estimates (78 cents vs. 87 cents expected) as gross margins fell 230 basis points year-over-year to 12.4%, well below the 13.85% Street estimate, despite revenue coming in slightly above at $2.311 billion vs. $2.17 billion expected. Management cited stubborn interest rates, elevated fuel costs, and inflationary pressure on household budgets as headwinds, and expects a relatively flat retail environment in fiscal 2027 without providing formal guidance. Some bright spots included healthy dealer inventory levels, structural cost-reduction actions underway, and a roughly 75% year-over-year surge in North American towable RV order backlog.

Viking Therapeutics shares surged in pre-market trading after reporting positive clinical trial results for its GLP-1 drug VK2735, showing 22% weight loss in trial participants. This is a significant data readout that validates VK2735 as a competitive candidate in the high-stakes GLP-1 weight loss drug market. The strong efficacy data could materially re-rate the stock and increase Viking's strategic value as a potential acquisition or partnership target.

sectors: The RV sector faces continued macro headwinds per THOR Industries commentary — stubborn interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation are suppressing retail demand. The GLP-1/obesity drug sector gets a positive catalyst from Viking's VK2735 data. Robotics and Physical AI M&A activity highlighted by the Cognex-RealSense deal.
tts_summary:
Good morning. Today's note is a company-specific earnings roundup for Tuesday, September 22nd — no broad macro or Fed commentary this morning, so let's get straight into the names.

Starting with the biggest mover: Viking Therapeutics is spiking in pre-market after reporting a 22% weight loss result from its GLP-1 drug VK2735. That is a standout efficacy number in a space dominated by Novo Nordisk and Eli Lilly. This data materially increases Viking's credibility and likely its value as an acquisition or partnership target. Watch this one closely at the open.

AutoZone beat on earnings — $56.05 versus the $54.03 consensus — but the quality is soft. The beat was almost entirely driven by tariff refunds, which added 145 basis points to gross margins, and a non-cash LIFO accounting benefit worth another 105 basis points. Strip those out and the picture is less impressive. Domestic same-store sales missed badly — up only 1.6% against the 3.1% expected — and operating expenses worsened. Management did note improving sales momentum in the back half of the quarter and said they feel well positioned for fiscal 2027 growth, but this is a low-quality beat and the stock should trade accordingly.

Cognex announced a roughly $500 million acquisition of RealSense, a leader in depth-sensing cameras for robotic perception and Physical AI applications. RealSense is growing revenue more than 50% year-over-year and expected to generate $80 to $90 million in sales. This is a strategic bet on the robotics and Physical AI buildout — a high-conviction growth area — and the deal looks well-targeted.

MillerKnoll beat expectations by a wide margin — 53 cents versus 36 cents — and importantly, even backing out the 11-cent tariff refund tailwind, they still would have beaten at 42 cents. Sales missed and organic revenue fell 3.3%, but orders rose and the earnings power is real. Fiscal 2027 EPS guidance was left unchanged. This is a solid print.

THOR Industries missed and the commentary was cautious. Gross margins fell 230 basis points below expectations, and management pointed to interest rates, fuel costs, and inflation squeezing household budgets through the key selling season. They expect flat retail in fiscal 2027. The bright spot is a 75% surge in North American towable RV order backlog, and management says structural cost cuts are designed to be durable, not temporary. Worth watching for stabilization.

Pentair announced a new CFO — Bob Hau, previously the finance chief at Fiserv, TE Connectivity, and Lennox — effective November 1st. Routine transition, no financial surprise.

Bottom line today: Viking is the high-conviction momentum trade on GLP-1 data. AutoZone's beat is not what it looks like on the surface. Cognex's acquisition looks strategically smart. Stay nimble.
